description: ∞-∞ at infinity involving a square root: multiply and divide by the conjugate to collapse the difference, then divide by the dominant power.

exercises.technique: ∞-∞ at infinity. Multiply and divide by the conjugate sqrt(x^2+x)+x to turn the difference into x/(sqrt(x^2+x)+x), then divide numerator and denominator by x and let x→∞.
∞-∞ at infinity. Multiply and divide by the conjugate sqrt(x^2+2x+3)+(x+1); the numerator collapses to the constant 2, so the whole expression is 2/[sqrt(x^2+2x+3)+x+1] → 0 as the denominator → ∞.

∞-∞ at negative infinity. Multiply and divide by the conjugate sqrt(x^2+9)-x: numerator collapses to the constant 9, giving 9/(sqrt(x^2+9)-x). As x→-∞, sqrt(x^2+9)~-x so the denominator → +∞, sending the ratio to 0.
